column1: # swarm manifest — single source of truth for what an `engineering-cto`
# swarm contains. Consumed by swarm-init.sh, swarm-sync.sh, and
# swarm-onboard.sh via manifest_walk in swarm-lib.sh, so first-stamp,
# upgrade, and onboard cannot diverge. Add a new artifact in ONE place: here.
# Per-type dispatch: at apply time, swarm_type_of() resolves a repo's
# archetype from its .claude/swarm-type marker (default 'engineering-cto')
# and the manifest at templates/<type>/manifest.tsv is consumed.
# Per-profile overlay (engineering-cto only, ADR-0013): an ORTHOGONAL
# .claude/swarm-profile marker (frontend|backend) appends a stack-specific
# overlay to the COMPOSED CLAUDE.md target ONLY. The overlay
# (templates/engineering-cto/profiles/<profile>/CLAUDE.md) is injected by
# manifest_apply_compose in swarm-lib.sh after the static sources when the
# fragment exists. An absent marker, or a label-only profile with no overlay
# fragment (v1 'backend' — today's engineering-cto already IS the backend
# case), appends nothing and composes byte-identically to a pre-profile swarm.
# Canon-mode overlay (engineering-cto only, see docs/CANON-MODES.md): an
# ORTHOGONAL .claude/canon-mode marker ('external'; absent/anything-else =
# 'local', the no-op default) appends two more sources to the COMPOSED
# CLAUDE.md target only: templates/engineering-cto/canon/CLAUDE.external-canon.md
# (shared external-canon doctrine) and then the repo-local
# .claude/canon-binding.md (names that repo's canon/spec repo; seeded by
# bin/swarm-canon-enable.sh). These, with the profile overlay, are the ONLY
# dynamically-sourced compose inputs and are deliberately NOT declared on the
# CLAUDE.md line below (which stays profile- and mode-agnostic). A markerless
# repo composes byte-identically to a pre-canon-mode swarm.
# Format: behavior | template-path | target-path [| covers]
#   - lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored
#   - fields are pipe-delimited, leading/trailing whitespace per field is trimmed
#   - covers (OPTIONAL 4th field): a terse one-line note of what topics the
#     target doc answers — the route-before-scan map. Hand-written here, next to
#     the line that already declares the file exists; no separate index, no
#     frontmatter, no generator. A reader routes by reading this column, opens
#     the named target, and only greps the tree as a fallback. A covered topic
#     with no matching `covers` note is incomplete-manifest, not a reason to
#     blind-grep — fix the note. manifest_walk absorbs `covers` into a catch-all
#     var and ignores it; it never affects target-path resolution.
#   - template-path is relative to $SWARM_HOME/templates/
#     (except seed-text, where this field is the literal text to seed)
#   - target-path is relative to the target repo
#     (except gitignore, where this field is .gitignore itself; the
#     template-path is the line we ensure is present in it)
# Behavior classes (each implemented as manifest_apply_<class> in swarm-lib.sh):
#   refresh     overwrite unconditionally (idempotent if cmp-equal); doctrine
#               and enforcement files that encode the operating contract
#   compose     concatenate '+'-joined sources LITERALLY (no separator
#               injected) into a tmp file, then refresh semantics against
#               the target. Each non-final source MUST end with at least
#               one '\n' so the seam is well-formed (see _base/README.md
#               for the trailing-newline invariant).
#   seed        copy only if absent in target; per-repo content the operator
#               (or CTO) authors after stamping. --force in init re-seeds.
#   seed-text   write literal text from template-path field into target, only
#               if absent. Same semantics as seed but for tiny inline content.
#   operator-owned
#               like seed (write-if-absent on init/onboard, never on sync)
#               but with one CRITICAL difference: --force does NOT re-seed.
#               For content the OPERATOR authors and owns (e.g. cpo
#               product-vision.md). swarm-init --force never clobbers it;
#               sync never touches it. SUBTREE SEMANTICS: an entry whose
#               target is `<dir>/.keep` declares the WHOLE `<dir>/`
#               subtree operator-owned — the manifest dispatcher refuses
#               ANY other entry that targets a path under that prefix
#               (regardless of class or --force flag), so future writes
#               under e.g. `products/` are a fatal manifest defect rather
#               than a silent clobber. The auto-stamped .claude/operator-
#               owned-paths list contains canonical entries (subtree
#               prefixes end in `/`, exact files do not) and is read by
#               the pre-commit hook (Layer 3) to refuse teammate-worktree
#               commits that stage anything matching. To reset operator-
#               owned content, the operator deletes the file by hand and
#               re-runs init.
#   settings    structured-merge swarm hook registrations + env + permissions
#               into the existing settings.json. Never clobber; additive +
#               dedup-by-command. See manifest_apply_settings.
#   git-hook    marker-aware: install if absent or existing has SWARM-MANAGED
#               marker; otherwise refuse (warn in init/sync, refuse with
#               COLLISION in onboard unless --force-precommit).
#   gitignore   append the line in template-path to .gitignore idempotently.
# behavior   | template-path                                                                                            | target-path

# Codex-native project layer. Command hooks are deliberately neutralized:
# Codex 0.144.x executes trusted hook commands outside its tool sandbox, and a
# definition hash does not make referenced repo scripts immutable. Keep an
# explicit empty hooks file so sync also disables unsafe older Qofi hook sets.
